sources.title: Large-scale whole-genome resequencing unravels the domestication history of Cannabis sativa
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed primary whole-genome study of 110 accessions. Central source for East Asian domestication model, ~12,000 BP divergence estimate, ~4,000 BP hemp/drug divergence, and selection signatures. The dating is model-based and carries a wide confidence interval.

sources.title: The origins of cannabis smoking: Chemical residue evidence from the first millennium BCE in the Pamirs
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed primary archaeological chemistry study. GC-MS of charred residues from wooden braziers at Jirzankal provides directly dated evidence for intentional burning of cannabis with a chemical profile consistent with relatively high psychoactive compounds around 500 BCE.

sources.title: Wild plant use and multi-cropping at the early Neolithic Zhuzhai site in the middle Yellow River region, China
sources.authors_or_org: Sheahan Bestel, Yingjian Bao, Hua Zhong, Xingcan Chen, Li Liu et al.
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed archaeobotanical excavation study. Supports chronology and context of early Neolithic plant remains at Zhuzhai. Later morphometric work discusses the cannabis seed from this site as larger than typical wild hemp, but its domesticated status should remain qualified.

sources.title: Cannabis in Eurasia: origin of human use and Bronze Age trans-continental connections
sources.authors_or_org: Tengwen Long, Mayke Wagner, Dieter Demske, Christian Leipe, Pavel E. Tarasov
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed systematic review of fibres, pollen, achenes and impressions across Eurasia. Useful for spread and for illustrating that the archaeological history is complex and may not fit a single simple center-of-use story.

sources.title: Morphometric approaches to Cannabis evolution and differentiation from archaeological sites: interpreting the archaeobotanical evidence from bronze age Haimenkou, Yunnan
sources.authors_or_org: Rita Dal Martello, Rui Min, Chris J. Stevens, Ling Qin, Dorian Q. Fuller
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed morphometric study including more than 800 archaeological cannabis grains from Haimenkou and a comparative dataset of modern and archaeological seeds. Functional inference from seed size is probabilistic, not a direct THC measurement.

sources.title: Integrating cannabis into the prehistoric crop assemblage: Phytolith evidence from Shandong, Northern China (4500-3400 BP)
sources.reliability_note: Recent peer-reviewed phytolith study from Beitaishang and Qianzhongzitou. Supports systematic integration of cannabis into Late Neolithic/Early Bronze Age agricultural contexts in Shandong. Because the study is recent and identification relies on phytolith criteria, use it as supporting evidence rather than the sole foundation for the origin date.

sources.title: A new insight into Cannabis sativa (Cannabaceae) utilization from 2500-year-old Yanghai Tombs, Xinjiang, China
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed archaeobotanical study identifying cannabis shoots, leaves and fruits from a 2500-year-old tomb. Ritual/medicinal function is contextual interpretation, so the script should not present function as chemically demonstrated.

sources.title: Whole-genome resequencing of wild and cultivated cannabis reveals the genetic structure and adaptive selection of important traits
sources.authors_or_org: Research team on Chinese wild and cultivated Cannabis
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed genomic study of Chinese wild and cultivated resources. Secondary support for selection on flowering time, seed and growth traits during domestication and for the distinct genetic structure of Chinese cannabis populations.

sources.title: Archaeobotanical evidence of the use of medicinal cannabis in a secular context unearthed from south China
sources.reliability_note: Peer-reviewed study of cannabis fruit remains from Han Dynasty Laoguanshan Cemetery. Useful only as later context; not necessary for the core domestication argument.

notes: Primary evidence was prioritized for core claims.
The ~12,000 BP domestication timing is a genomic demographic estimate, not a single excavated date.
The script must preserve uncertainty around early independent cultivation, exact center of domestication, seed-based functional inference and the meaning of basal/feral populations.
